1 5:04 What physical changes do we usually experience when under pressure??Our heart starts pounding, we breathe faster, and we may start sweating.
2 5:12 How do we tend to interpret these changes??We usually interpret them as anxiety or as signs that we are not coping with the pressure.
3 5:20 How could we view them instead??As signs that the body is energised and preparing us to meet a challenge.
4 5:40 What were the participants of the study told to do??They were taught to rethink their stress response as something helpful — for example, a pounding heart preparing them for action.
5 5:55 How did the participants who viewed stress as helpful feel??They were less stressed out, less anxious, and more confident.
6 6:04 What is a typical stress response??Your heart rate goes up and your blood vessels constrict.
7 6:12 What toll could chronic stress have on you??It can lead to cardiovascular disease because the body stays in this constricted state too often.
8 6:32 How did the group of participants who viewed stress as helpful respond physically??Their blood vessels stayed relaxed, even though their hearts were still pounding — a much healthier cardiovascular profile.
9 6:52 What does the new science of stress reveal??That how you think about stress really matters and can change how your body responds to it.
10 7:00 How did her goal change as a psychologist??She no longer wants to get rid of people's stress — she wants to make them better at handling it.
11 7:08 What could have saved the lives of those who experience lots of stress??Learning to see their stress response as the body helping them rise to a challenge.
12 7:28 On what condition does our stress response become healthier??When we view stress as helpful rather than harmful — when the body "believes" us, the response itself changes.
